article.summary: AutoResearchClaw is a research-paper pipeline with a local JSONL memory library, a separate run-scoped lesson store, and an optional lesson-to-skill bridge. The review reports source observations only; the system and benchmarks were not run.

who_what.text: The public repository is under the aiming-lab GitHub organization. Its README describes AutoResearchClaw as an open-source research-paper pipeline with optional human guidance and integrations. The memory library is a supporting repository subsystem, not a separately hosted memory service.

The README describes optional MetaClaw cross-run lesson-to-skill transfer; the integration guide documents the bridge setup and workflow. Repository descriptions are documentation observations, not performance findings.

architecture.text: MemoryEntry records an ID, one of three categories, content, free-form metadata, embedding, confidence, created/access times, and access count. MemoryStore keeps category lists in memory and persists ideation.jsonl, experiment.jsonl, and writing.jsonl.

The separate EvolutionStore appends stage, category, severity, description, timestamp, and run ID lesson objects to run-local evolution/lessons.jsonl. Stage prompt assembly can read those lessons plus up to five arc-* skills from the configured MetaClaw skills directory.

The default MemoryConfig names .researchclaw/memory, caps each category at 500, and configures a 90-day decay half-life and confidence threshold 0.3. The pipeline runner separately creates a run-local experiment_memory directory for the experiment wrapper.

When the optional bridge is enabled, its post-run hook can generate skill files from sufficiently severe lessons; the default bridge is disabled. The shared skills directory is the source-visible cross-run persistence path, separate from run-local EvolutionStore lessons.

behavior.text: MemoryStore.add validates the category, creates an ID and timestamps, appends an entry, and enforces the per-category cap by keeping higher-confidence entries. update_confidence clamps to [0, 1]; mark_accessed updates timestamp and count. prune removes low-confidence or over-age entries. Save rewrites full JSONL category files and load skips malformed rows. No edit-content or delete-by-ID method appears in the inspected store.

MemoryRetriever scores category-selected entries using weighted cosine similarity, exponential age decay, confidence, and normalized access frequency, then sorts and returns top-k. Text recall needs an embedding callback; absent one, it logs and returns no results. Retrieved entries are marked accessed.

EmbeddingProvider selects a configured OpenAI-compatible embedding endpoint, sentence-transformers when installed, or a 256-dimensional hashed-token TF-IDF fallback. API failures fall back to TF-IDF. This describes branches visible in source, not their runtime availability or quality.

ExperimentMemory.__init__ takes a MemoryStore and MemoryRetriever, but the pipeline runner constructs it with store_dir=. The call is inside an exception handler, so source inspection indicates initialization is skipped for this hook. The subsequent runner hook also imports ExperimentOutcome and calls record_outcome, neither of which is defined in the inspected experiment_memory.py; errors are caught and recording is skipped. These are static mismatches; no runtime execution was performed.

EvolutionStore appends lesson JSONL rows and can query recent lessons for a stage with recency and severity weighting. The runner extracts and appends lessons under that run directory; prompt assembly reads that directory and can add arc-* skills from the shared configured skills path. The lesson store has append/read/query behavior and no general update or delete API in the inspected code.

The optional bridge filters lessons by severity, asks an LLM to create skills, sanitizes skill names, and writes SKILL.md directories. The current source caps the conversion count by max_skills; prompt assembly reads at most five arc-* skills. The bridge config defaults to disabled, so these cross-run skill actions depend on configuration.

Direct MemoryEntry metadata can include caller-supplied run IDs but has no user, tenant, or enforced principal scope field. Run-local evolution directories and the shared skills directory have different scope boundaries; category filtering is not authorization.

Memory and lesson records carry IDs, time, category, confidence/severity, and run context, but the inspected paths do not attach a verified source passage or adjudicate whether stored content is supported. Generated skills are LLM-authored guidance rather than source citations.

metrics.evidence: Similarity-ranked retrieval is visible in source, but no answerable recall or abstention workload was measured.
Confidence updates exist, but no content correction path or stale-value evaluation was measured.
Pruning removes entries by confidence/age, but no deletion completeness or leakage probe was run.
Categories and run directories are visible, but no tenant isolation boundary or cross-scope probe was verified.
Records carry context metadata, but no claim-to-source evidence model or support-precision workload was measured.
The source uses in-memory list scans and file persistence; no retrieval latency distribution or write-to-recall delay was collected.
Embedding backends and prompt character bounds are source-visible, but no token, provider cost, or storage workload was measured.

limits.text: This bounded review inspected the current README and integration guide, memory store/retriever/embedding modules, specialized wrappers, pipeline runner and prompt assembly, EvolutionStore, and the lesson-to-skill bridge at the verified SHA.

The code was not executed and no tests or benchmarks were run. Static call mismatches, deployed configuration, runtime isolation, retrieval quality, deletion completeness, and real cost/performance remain unverified.

The official README and pinned SECURITY.md and SUPPORT.md paths were checked for a published contact email. No project contact email was published; the README's noreply address is an OpenAlex configuration example and was not treated as contact information.

benchmark.text: Benchmark not run. No AutoResearchClaw memory path, system workload, tests, or benchmark was executed. Project metrics, status, and fixture are protocol artifacts, not findings about this system.
